name: CA-50
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Scott Peters holds a massive financial edge: $2.57M cash on hand versus about $2,000 for Steve Cohen
The district's partisan lean favors Democrats by 10 points
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 96 percent
No public polls or expert ratings exist, so fundamentals carry the forecast
model.rationale: A D+10 district, a well-funded two-term incumbent, and a challenger who has raised only about $4,000 all point the same direction, and markets price the race near 96 percent Democratic. With no polling suggesting otherwise, the fundamentals-based margin of roughly 21 points stands.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending against Peters or a sharp shift in the national environment would be the most plausible way this margin narrows.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Scott Peters, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a San Diego-area district that leans Democratic by about ten points. He enters the general election with roughly $2.6 million on hand after raising more than $2.1 million, while Republican Steve Cohen has reported about $4,000 raised and $2,000 in the bank. No outside groups are spending against Peters, and prediction markets price his chances near 96 percent.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on district partisanship, incumbency, and the stark fundraising gap. Those fundamentals point to a comfortable Democratic win, with the main uncertainty being how a barely funded challenger performs in a low-information contest. A significant change in the national political climate or unexpected outside spending would be the most plausible source of movement.
